Facts: Heirs brought a judicial division action with cumulative claims seeking declaration of relative simulation of a sale allegedly concealing a donation, reduction for infringement of the reserved share, and collation of inter vivos donations, concerning the estates of two deceased parents; the defendant resisted and raised counterclaims.

Legal framework
Articles 50-bis, 132, 183, 263, 785 CPC on composition of the court, judgments, division proceedings and ancillary disputes; Articles 536, 542, 554–556, 560, 564, 581, 737, 770 ICC on forced heirs, reduction, fictitious reconstitution, acceptance with benefit of inventory, imputation, collation and customary gifts; settled Supreme Court case law on holographic wills, burden of proof in reduction actions, simulation, and pretermitted heirs.

Interpretative issue
Whether the action for reduction was admissible in the absence of specific allegations and proof of the estate’s value and the extent of the alleged lesion; whether heirs could prove relative simulation of a sale without a successful reduction action; whether pretermitted heirs or their successors could seek collation; and whether a holographic will could be invalidated through generic objections.

Principle applied
The action for reduction requires strict compliance with the burden of allegation and proof: the claimant must specifically indicate the estate, its value at the opening of succession, the reserved share, the extent of the lesion, the impugned acts, and must impute prior donations to the reserved share; court-appointed expertise cannot remedy deficiencies in pleadings. Failure to meet these requirements renders the action inadmissible. A forced heir may rely on testimonial and presumptive evidence to prove simulation of a sale concealing a donation only if a well-founded reduction action is brought; otherwise, simulation must be proven exclusively by written counter-declaration. A pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only after a successful reduction judgment and, until then, lacks standing to seek division or collation. Collation operates solely among co-heirs and is distinct from reduction; exemption from collation must be expressly or unequivocally inferred from the deceased’s will. The authenticity of a holographic will must be challenged through an action for negative verification, with the burden of proof on the challenger; generic allegations of falsity or vitiated consent are insufficient. ; Type_of_succession: Testamentary; Second part of full text: Therefore, the burden of allegation and proof that was placed on the plaintiffs, established in the maxims of solid case law, cannot be fulfilled through the advice of the judge's assistant.

Furthermore, Article 564, paragraph 2, of the Civil Code provides, in addition to prior acceptance with the benefit of inventory, a further condition for the exercise of the action for reduction: the legitimate heir must attribute to his or her reserved share the legacies and donations made in his or her favour by the deceased (◻.In any case, the legitimate heir who requests the reduction of donations (Article 555 of the Italian Civil Code) or testamentary dispositions (Article 554 of the Italian Civil Code) must attribute the donations and legacies made to him to his legitimate portion, unless he has been expressly exempted (Articles 552, 553, and 724 of the Italian Civil Code).

This obligation is necessary, as it is intended to prevent the heir from asserting their right to a legitimate share even for the part already satisfied by the deceased through acts of generosity, and it only ceases to apply if the heir has been expressly exempted by the deceased (Article 564, second paragraph of the Civil Code), so much so that, for the purposes of exercising and accepting the action for reduction, the exemption from collation does not extend to imputation.

The plaintiffs merely alleged that in 1986 **HEIR 4** and **THE DECEASED** had donated part of the property to **HEIR 3** without formally imputing the share due to the legitimate heir, even though there was no waiver, as can be inferred from the deed of donation.

The failure to impute the aforementioned donation is, moreover, also admitted by the plaintiffs themselves, who stated in their brief 183, sixth paragraph, no. 1) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure: 'the fact that the plaintiff did not impute the share received by donation from his father is certainly not an indication of inadmissibility...' (page 5 of the brief pursuant to Article 183, paragraph 6, no. 1) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure).

Therefore, the action for reduction must be declared inadmissible and, consequently, any claim relating to the return of the assets must be rejected.

On the claim of simulation relating to the sale of 5 January 2001.

The claim of simulation relating to the sale of 5 January 2001, entered into between **HEIR 4** and his son **HEIR 2**, is instrumental to the action for reduction.

The legitimate heir, who asserts in court his personal right to the intangibility of the legitimate portion and who requests the reinstatement of the reserved portion, is considered a third party with respect to the simulated agreement, since, in this case, he is acting to protect his own right (the right to the intangibility of the reserved portion).

Consequently, "The legitimate heir who requests a declaration of simulation of a sale made by the deceased, aimed at concealing, in reality, a donation, acts to

Page18 of 30

protection of his own right and is a third party with respect to the contracting parties, so that testimonial and presumptive evidence is admissible without limitation when, on the premise that the simulated act involves a reduction in his reserved share, he proposes, at the same time as the action for simulation, a request for reduction of the concealed donation, aimed at having the asset declared part of the estate and his share calculated taking into account the asset itself" (Court of Cassation, Section 2, Judgment No. 19912 of 22/09/2014).

Case law is absolutely consistent and coherent in allowing the (legitimate) heir, in his capacity as a legitimate heir, to act simultaneously in simulation and reduction for the protection of the right to the intangibility of the legitimate portion, to have access to testimonial and presumptive evidence of the simulation agreement in the same way as a third party with respect to the parties who have initiated the simulation proceedings.

That said, it is clear that the close interconnection between the action for reduction and the claim of simulation of a solemn act, such as to allow the person acting in reduction to be admitted to witness evidence, means that the procedural outcome of the latter depends on whether or not the former is upheld.

Therefore, if the action for reduction is not upheld, the legitimate heir cannot be considered a third party and therefore cannot be admitted to testimonial and presumptive evidence.

The simulation will in fact (in the absence of confession and oath) be subject only to documentary evidence by attaching the written text of the simulation agreement (so-called counter-declaration).

In this case, such evidence may be provided by means of texts only in the event of the innocent loss of the document.

It follows that in the case in question, the claim of relative simulation must be rejected because no proof of the actual simulation agreement has been found, whereby the parties would have actually intended to conceal a donation.

On the obligation of collation.

The plaintiffs requested that the court ascertain the existence of the defendant's obligation to collate all the immovable and movable property received by him as a donation and, consequently, order him to transfer it to the estate.

The defendant objected to the admissibility of the request for collation, as it was subject to the acceptance of the request for verification of simulation and verification of the infringement of the legitimate share reserved for **HEIR 3**. Furthermore, in order for

Page19 of 30

collation can proceed, there must be a relictum in addition to the donatum. The former, in light of the plaintiffs' allegations, is absent, because **HEIR 4** died without leaving any assets.

Collation is the act by which the descendants and spouse who accept the inheritance contribute to the estate what they have received from the deceased as a gift.

Collation is based on the assessment that what the deceased has donated to the necessary heirs must be considered an advance on the inheritance and, therefore, this institution aims to remove the disparities in treatment that donations would create between co-heirs.

Collation should not be understood as a tool for reinstating the legitimate portion, even if it may in fact achieve the result of eliminating any damage to the reserved portions caused by acts of generosity carried out by the deceased.

The persons required to make collation are the spouse and descendants who are co-heirs, i.e. who have accepted the inheritance; legitimate heirs who are not co-heirs are not required to make collation until they have successfully brought an action for reduction and obtained the status of heir. Only an action for reduction may be brought against them, if the conditions are met.

That said, in the present case, two successions are relevant, which, for the purposes of the claims for collation, must be analysed separately: on the one hand, the succession of **HEIR 4**, which opened on 27 October 2003 upon his death; on the other hand, the succession of **THE DECEASED**, which opened on 1 February 2000.

The above can be inferred from the following elements:

- the plaintiffs have requested recognition of the defendant's obligation to collate all donations received by him, including those made by his mother;

- they requested that the estate be divided as determined at the time of the opening of the succession;

- in this regard, the writ of summons states 'at the time of the opening of the succession', but the plaintiffs in brief no. 1) pursuant to Article 183 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure specified 'to determine, at the time of the opening of the succession, the estate';

- the reference to both successions can be inferred, in any case, from a systematic reading of the writ of summons, which requests the dissolution of the joint ownership

Page20 of 30

still existing between the siblings (5/6 for brother **HEIR 2** and 1/6 for the heirs of **HEIR 3**) of the property located in M. inherited following the death of their mother **THE DECEASED**;

- The defendant assumed that both successions were the subject of the proceedings. In fact, in its conclusions in the statement of defence and reply, it requested: 'to proceed with the collation of the donation made in favour of Mr **HEIR 3** and, consequently, with the division of the determined joint inheritance, devolving, with regard to the succession of **THE DECEASED** (50%), 1/3 to Mr **HEIR 3** and 1/3 to Mr **HEIR 2** as legitimate heirs and, with regard to the succession of **HEIR 4** (4/6), the 1/3 share to the heirs of **HEIR 3**..." (page 15 of the statement of defence and reply);

- therefore, all parties requested the collation and division of the joint inheritance in relation to both inheritances;

- consequently, the Court, based on the principle of correspondence between what is requested and what is pronounced, will have to examine and rule on both successions.

With regard to the succession of **HEIR 4**, it appears that:

- This is a testamentary succession by virtue of the holographic will signed by the deceased on 6 July 2000, published by the notary on 8 January 2009, recognised as authentic and valid (see grounds in paragraph 'On the falsity of the holographic will of **HEIR 4** dated 6 July 2000' of this judgment);

- in the aforementioned will, the deceased disposed of all his movable and immovable property, assigning it to his son **HEIR 2**;

- this is a disposition attributing the entirety of the estate, therefore universally representing the appointment of **HEIR 2** as heir;

- the son **HEIR 3**, consequently, can be considered a legitimate heir totally pretermitted by the universal disposition, regardless of the donation received during his parents' lifetime;

- indeed, by virtue of that donation, he was exclusively a donee, while the status of heir is acquired with the call to inheritance at the time of the opening of the succession;

- with the sale on 5 January 2001, he transferred the bare ownership, reserving the usufruct, to his son **HEIR 2** of 4/6 of the property located in M., via (omissis...), thus disposing of all his real estate assets;

Page21 of 30

- the deceased was the holder of current account no. (omissis...) at the CRC, Montignoso Branch, on which the defendant had power of attorney with separate signature to carry out banking transactions;

- this circumstance was not disputed by the defendant, but was admitted on page 16 of the closing statement ('These amounts were paid in full into deposit book no. 0 (omissis...), held by the second (**HEIR 4**, editor's note) and with separate signing authority granted to the former, as shown in the deposit slips presented by Cassa di Risparmio di Carrara on 23 October 2000 and 8 January 2000', page 16 of the closing statement);

- at the time of **HEIR 4**'s death, this savings account had been emptied, with only €40.82 remaining on 24 March 2004 (document 6 in the plaintiff's file), but the plaintiffs claim that, prior to the withdrawals made by **HEIR 2**, the balance amounted to €62,548.94;

- Finally, **HEIR 4** had inherited from his wife, **THE DECEASED**, 1/3 of the sum contained in passbook no. 421844 at the CRC, Montignoso Agency, which on 7 March 2000 amounted to 13,969 lire (doc. 5, plaintiff's file).

- the withdrawals of money from the savings accounts were admitted by the defendant, who justified them on the grounds of the need to meet the needs and maintenance of his parents, as well as for the improvement and maintenance of the properties available to them;

- the records show several withdrawals from the account (omissis...): on 27 November 2000, a withdrawal of 5,000,000 lire; on 28 May 2001, a withdrawal of 5,000,000 lire; on 30 April 2001 a withdrawal of 6,000,000 lire, but there is also a deposit of 40,000,000 lire by **HEIR 2**, by means of cheques from Monte dei Paschi di Siena;

That said, the Supreme Court of Cassation has consistently held that a pretermitted heir cannot bring an action for collation:

"In matters of inheritance, a pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only after successfully exercising the right of reduction; it follows that, prior to this moment, he or she cannot request the division of the estate or the collation of assets, since both of these rights presuppose the assumption of the status of heir and the joint attribution of an inheritance." (Civil Cassation, Section II, 13/01/2010, no. 368);

"The pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only from the moment of the judgment granting his or her claim for reduction, removing the preclusive effect of the testamentary provisions prejudicial to the legitimate portion, which are not in themselves null and void or voidable;

Page22 of 30

it follows that, prior to the acceptance of the request for reduction, the pretermitted heir is not entitled to succeed the deceased in the legal proceedings initiated by the latter, as he or she cannot be qualified as a universal successor within the meaning of Article 110 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure." (Civil Cassation, Section I, 20/11/2008, no. 27556);

"The pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only from the moment of the judgment granting his or her request for reduction, removing the preclusive effect of the testamentary dispositions. It follows that, prior to the acceptance of the request for reduction, the pretermitted heir is not entitled to succeed the deceased in the legal proceedings initiated by the latter, since the only person entitled to continue the proceedings, pursuant to Article 110 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, is the universal successor." (Civil Cassation, Section III, 12/01/1999, no. 251).

Therefore, applying the principle established by case law, it follows that:

- the heirs of **HEIR 3** are not entitled to request collation, as their ascendant was a pretermitted heir and the action for reduction brought by them (in their capacity as sole heirs of the same) was unsuccessful, meaning that they did not acquire the status of co-heirs;

- therefore, the claim for collation brought by the plaintiffs must be rejected.

The counterclaim brought by the defendant **HEIR 2** concerning the collation of the donation made by the parents in 1986 in favour of his brother **HEIR 3** must be rejected, again with reference to the paternal succession, as it is subject to the acceptance of the plaintiffs' claim for collation.

Therefore, this claim is absorbed by the rejection of the claims brought by the plaintiffs.

Furthermore, it should be noted that the pretermitted heir is not subject to the obligation of collation, as he is not a co-heir (Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code).

With regard to the sums of money withdrawn by **HEIR 2**, it should be noted that the will attributed to him all immovable and movable property, including, therefore, the sums of money held by the deceased.

Therefore, if the plaintiffs considered themselves to have been harmed in their legitimate share by their father's testamentary dispositions, in order to recover the sums of money contained in the current accounts for the estate, they should have requested, in a counterclaim and, alternatively, the reduction of the testamentary disposition considered harmful (a request that they did not make, on which it is not possible to decide, in accordance with the principle of party disposition and the party's initiative that governs civil proceedings).

Page23 of 30

On the testamentary succession of **THE DECEASED**. **THE DECEASED** died intestate on 01.02.2000.

At the opening of the succession, the legitimate co-heirs were: the husband **HEIR 4** and the children, **HEIR 2** and **HEIR 3** (Article 565 of the Italian Civil Code).

Based on the joint inheritance of the spouse and children (in the legitimate or ex lege succession), **HEIR 4** was entitled to 1/3 of **THE DECEASED**'s estate, while the two children were entitled to 2/3, i.e. 1/3 each of their mother's estate (◻.( if children are entitled to the same share as the spouse, the spouse is entitled to half of the inheritance if only one child is entitled to the inheritance, and to one third in other cases' (Article 581 of the Italian Civil Code).

**THE DECEASED**'s estate was composed as follows:

- 1/2 of the full ownership of the building identified in the urban land registry, sheet (omissis...), cat. A/2, cl. 1, located in M. via (omissis...) (the other half was owned by her husband **HEIR 4**);

- 1/3 of the ownership of the balance in the registered savings account no. (omissis...) opened at the Cassa di Risparmio di Carrara, Montignoso Branch, in the name of **THE DECEASED**, as well as his children **HEIR 2** and **HEIR 3**.

Half of the full ownership of the above property was therefore inherited by the spouse and children, each receiving 1/3 by virtue of the joint ownership of the spouse and children (1/3 to the husband and 2/3 to the two children, to be divided equally between them, i.e. 1/3 to each child).

The shares were therefore as follows:

- **HEIR 4** was the owner of the remaining half of the property, to which was added, following the succession of his wife's share, the fraction of 1/3, so he was the owner of 4/6 of the building in Via (omissis...) (1/2 + 1/3 = 4/6);

- the children **HEIR 3** and **HEIR 2** were therefore owners of 1/6 each.

With the deed of sale dated 05.01.2001 before the notary, Repertory no. (omissis...) Collection no. (omissis...), Registered in Ma. on (omissis...). and Transcribed on 11.01.2001, **HEIR 4** sold to his son **HEIR 2** "the bare ownership share of four sixths (4/6)" of the property registered at parcel (omissis...), cat. A/2, cl. (omissis...), via (omissis...), reserving the usufruct and thus disposing of all his real estate assets.

Therefore, upon his death, **HEIR 2** became the full owner of 4/6 of the aforementioned building, to which was added his share (derived from his mother's inheritance) of 1/6, for a total share of 5/6.

Page24 of 30

This property remains jointly owned by **HEIR 2** (owner of 5/6) and the heirs of **HEIR 3** for the share belonging to the latter (1/6).

With regard to the joint account no. (omissis...) opened at the Cassa di Risparmio di Carrara, Montignoso Branch, it is clear that **HEIR 3** was entitled, by virtue of legitimate succession, to 1/3 of the sum belonging to his mother (who in turn owned 1/3 of the entire sum).

Consequently, with regard to the residual maternal succession, there remains a situation of joint ownership and therefore a relictum represented by the property located in Via (omissis...) in Montignoso and the sums contained in the savings account.

The plaintiffs have expressly requested the dissolution of the joint ownership of the building identified in the urban land registry, sheet (omissis...), cat. A/2, cl. 1, located in Mo. via (omissis...) ('with reference to this property, the dissolution of the joint inheritance is requested', page 6 of the writ of summons), subject to collation of the donations made in favour of the defendant.

It is considered that the conditions for the request for division of the inheritance, as well as for the request for collation, are met, in that, with regard to the maternal succession:

- **HEIR 3** and **HEIR 2** were co-heirs by virtue of legitimate succession;

- In the mother's inheritance, there is a relictum represented by the property located in Via (omissis...) in Montignoso and the credit balance of joint account no. (omissis...);

- the descendants are entitled to request collation.

Therefore, **HEIR 2** is obliged to make a collation with reference only to the donation made during the lifetime of **THE DECEASED** (together with her husband **HEIR 4**): in particular, the donation of 07.07.1986 before the notary in Massa, Repertory no. (omissis...)., Transcribed in Massa on (omissis...)., in favour of **HEIR 2** concerning 'the entire second floor of the building in Via (omissis...), consisting of a living room, three bedrooms, kitchen and toilet, with exclusive ownership of the entire attic above the flat, a portion of the basement used as a cellar and a portion of land used as a garden located upstream; with co-ownership of the staircase leading to the first floor and ownership of the staircase from the first floor to the attic" listed in the N.C.E.U. under entry (omissis...), fg. (omissis...) (doc. 3 plaintiff's file).

Consequently, **HEIR 2** is required to contribute this property, received as a gift, to the estate. Furthermore, since this property has not been sold or mortgaged, as in the present case, the contributor has the choice between contribution in kind (consisting of the

Page25 of 30

returning the right to the estate) or contribution by imputation (consisting of paying the value of the property).

In this regard, the objections raised by the defendant must be rejected.

In particular, the objection that 'the will must be understood as exempting the latter (**HEIR 2**, editor's note) from the collation of gifts received' is unfounded.

The heir is required to collate the donations, unless he has been exempted by the deceased whose estate is in question. The exemption is an accessory transaction to the donation (contemporary or subsequent), which must take the same form; or it may be contained in a will.

First of all, this concerns the succession of **THE DECEASED**, so the dispensation had to come from the deceased and a dispensation issued by another person cannot be considered valid.

In any case, the will does not contain any express exemption from the obligation of collation and, even if the exemption may also be tacit, it must be able to be inferred unequivocally. For example, the testator should have expressed the obligation solely to his son **HEIR 2**, as can be inferred from the following maxim in terms: 'In the field of negotiation, in order to have a tacit manifestation of the will of a party, 'facta concludentia' are required, i.e. unambiguous and unequivocal, incompatible with a will contrary to that which is argued from it. Such incompatibility does not have to be logical and absolute, as may be given by the principle of contradiction, it being sufficient that it be practical and relative, as results from the predominant concept in practical business life. (In application of the principle referred to in the maxim, the Supreme Court upheld the decision of the trial judge who affirmed the tacit exemption from the obligation of collation of a property by an heir on the grounds that in the same will, this obligation of collation was expressly imposed on another co-heir)" (Civil Cassation, Section II, 08/11/1983, no. 6591).

In light of this jurisprudential principle, elements external to the will reveal an intention that is far from consistent with the decision to exempt the son **HEIR 2** from including the donation received in 1986 in the estate.

Indeed, the fact that two donations were made on that occasion (one to their son **HEIR 3** and one to their son **HEIR 2**) indicates that the deceased did not wish to assign the donated property to **HEIR 2** as an additional benefit on top of his share of the legitimate inheritance.

Finally, the heirs of **HEIR 3** are also required to include in the estate the donation received from their deceased in 1986 concerning 'the entire first floor of the building in

Page26 of 30

via (omissis...), consisting of a living room, three bedrooms, kitchen and toilet, with ownership of a portion of the basement used as a cellar and a portion of land used as a garden facing the sea; with co-ownership of the staircase leading to the basement and co-ownership of the portion of land used as a car park' identified in the N.C.E.U. under entry (omissis...) (doc. 3 plaintiff's file).

In fact, the heirs of **HEIR 3**, as legitimate co-heirs together with his brother **HEIR 2** in the maternal succession, are obliged to make a collation (Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code).

On the action for rendering of accounts brought by the plaintiffs.

In the conclusions of the writ of summons, the plaintiffs requested 'the determination, at the time of the opening of the succession, of the estate to be divided, including the accounting of the assets enjoyed by the defendant' (page 8 of the writ of summons).

In particular, they requested an account of the attic of the property in Via (omissis...), which was the subject of the 1986 donation and which, in theory, is a genuine attic floor, which the defendant allegedly enjoyed by renting it to third parties (page 4 of the writ of summons).

With regard to the property sold by **HEIR 4** to his son **HEIR 2**, there is no obligation to provide an account, since, having rejected the claim of simulation, this act must be considered a sale and, therefore, ownership has been transferred and the owner can freely enjoy the property (which is therefore not part of the estate to be divided: the account is in fact instrumental to the division of the estate).

That said, in general terms with regard to the request for an account, the following should be noted:

- first of all, the accounting can only be decided by judgment when the court has already (in the case of an undisputed obligation to account) ordered the obligated party (or parties) to file the statement of account (and the supporting documentation for the assets and liabilities) at least five days before the hearing set for the discussion of the account, at that hearing the party requesting the statement of account has declared that it does not accept it, fulfilling the obligation to indicate the specific items contested and the specific reasons for the contestation, and, at the end of the discussion, the parties have not reached any agreement;

- in the present proceedings, the court has not yet had the opportunity to order any of the parties concerned to file the statement of account and related documentation, so that the proceedings referred to in Article 263 et seq. of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure have not yet commenced;

Page27 of 30

- in accordance with the same Article 723 of the Italian Civil Code, invoked: "After the sale, if it has taken place, of movable or immovable property, the accounts that the co-owners must render shall be settled";

- the same provision, therefore, postpones the rendering of accounts until the conclusion of the sale transactions (where ordered: i.e., in the case of indivisibility in kind of the property and in any case at the request of a party);

- this postponement of the incidental accounting procedure until the conclusion of the sale transactions in the main proceedings for division is shared by specialist doctrine on the subject of divisions;

- consequently, it is necessary to appoint a court-appointed expert to not only estimate the market value of the properties comprising the estate but also to assess whether or not they are divisible in kind and, if so, to draw up a plan for division in kind:

- in the event of indivisibility, in kind, of the estate, the court shall order, solely and exclusively at the request of a party, a judicial sale (which shall follow the new rules that recently came into force in August 2015) and shall appoint a professional to carry out the sale and to take custody of the properties subject to the sale;

- upon completion of the sale, the reconstruction of the estate to be divided shall be completed by means of an incidental accounting procedure, which may result in a negative, positive or zero balance;

- in the event of a specific dispute over the accounting and a persistent lack of agreement even after the hearing to discuss it, the accounting procedure (if any) that has been repeatedly disputed must be settled by means of a judgment;

- the outcome will be the distribution of any remaining assets among the parties involved.

For the reasons set out above, the following ruling does not contain any specific provision relating to the aforementioned request for an account, which is to be understood as included in the provision in which the Court issues, by separate order, separate measures for the investigation of the case.

That said, with regard to the request for division of the inherited assets made by the plaintiff and also requested by the defendants, it will nevertheless be essential to refer the case back to the preliminary investigation stage for the appointment of a new court-appointed expert in order to form the estate, subject to collation by the parties of the two donations made by the deceased on 7 July 1986, relating to the succession of **THE DECEASED**. Consequently, a division plan must be drawn up, on which the parties must agree in accordance with Articles 788 or 789 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure

Page28 of 30

also evaluating possible conciliatory solutions in light of the provisions of this non-definitive ruling.

Publication of this judgment.

This judgment is not subject to transcription as the claim for simulation and the claim for reduction have not been upheld.

Legal costs.

In accordance with the so-called "principle of globality", despite the fact that this partially final judgment is, in itself, sufficient to give rise to liability for costs, the legal costs cannot be settled here, but only at the end of the proceedings, as part of an overall assessment of liability.

P.Q.M.

The Ordinary Court of Massa, Single Civil Section, sitting as a panel, definitively ruling with a partial judgment in the civil case referred to above, rejecting any contrary or different claim, petition, action, exception, deduction and defence:

- REJECTS the request to declare 'non-existent, inauthentic, ineffective and null and void and/or voidable the testamentary provisions and specifically that dated 6 July 2000 and published on 8 January 2009 attached by the defendant', to be understood as referring to the holographic will drawn up by **HEIR 4** on 6 July 2000 and published on 8 January 2009 in Massa, with minutes no. (omissis...) of the Repertory and no. 12221 of the Collection, by the notary, registered with the Notarial Association of the United Districts of La Spezia and Massa, proposed in the brief filed on 19 March 2009 pursuant to Article 183, paragraph 6, no. 1 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure by the plaintiffs;

- ACCERTA and, to that effect, DECLARES that the plaintiffs, as heirs who "come to the succession in place" of the "legitimate heir" **HEIR 3**, have been completely omitted from the holographic will, drawn up by **HEIR 4** on 06.07.2000 and published on 8.01.2009 in Massa, with minutes no. (omissis...) of the Repertory and no. 12221 of the Collection, by the notary, a notary registered with the Notarial Association of the United Districts of La Spezia and Massa;

- DECLARES inadmissible the request for reduction made by the plaintiffs **HEIR 1, HEIR 1, HEIR 1** and **HEIR 1** against **HEIR 2** inadmissible;

Page29 of 30

- REJECTS the request for verification and declaration of the relative simulation of the sale dated 05.01.2001;

- DECLARES inadmissible the claim for collation made by the plaintiffs with respect to the estate of **HEIR 4** and, as a result, REJECTS the counterclaim for collation brought by the defendant against the plaintiffs;

- FIND and, as a result, DECLARE that the plaintiffs, with reference to the estate of **THE DECEASED**, are required to collate the donation dated 7 July 1986 concerning the building registered and identified in the N.C.E.U. under entry (omissis...) and that the defendant is required to collate the donation dated 07.07.1986 concerning the building identified in the N.C.E.U. under the entry (omissis...), fg. (omissis...);

- COSTS at the end of the proceedings;

- ISSUES, by separate order, separate measures for further investigation of the case.

So decided on 07.06.2016 in the council chamber of the Ordinary Court of Massa, Single Civil Section, in the collegiate composition specified in the epigraph.; law: Divorce

Therefore, the burden of allegation and proof that was placed on the plaintiffs, established in the maxims of solid case law, cannot be fulfilled through the advice of the judge's assistant.

Furthermore, Article 564, paragraph 2, of the Civil Code provides, in addition to prior acceptance with the benefit of inventory, a further condition for the exercise of the action for reduction: the legitimate heir must attribute to his or her reserved share the legacies and donations made in his or her favour by the deceased (◻.In any case, the legitimate heir who requests the reduction of donations (Article 555 of the Italian Civil Code) or testamentary dispositions (Article 554 of the Italian Civil Code) must attribute the donations and legacies made to him to his legitimate portion, unless he has been expressly exempted (Articles 552, 553, and 724 of the Italian Civil Code).

This obligation is necessary, as it is intended to prevent the heir from asserting their right to a legitimate share even for the part already satisfied by the deceased through acts of generosity, and it only ceases to apply if the heir has been expressly exempted by the deceased (Article 564, second paragraph of the Civil Code), so much so that, for the purposes of exercising and accepting the action for reduction, the exemption from collation does not extend to imputation.

The plaintiffs merely alleged that in 1986 **HEIR 4** and **THE DECEASED** had donated part of the property to **HEIR 3** without formally imputing the share due to the legitimate heir, even though there was no waiver, as can be inferred from the deed of donation.

The failure to impute the aforementioned donation is, moreover, also admitted by the plaintiffs themselves, who stated in their brief 183, sixth paragraph, no. 1) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure: 'the fact that the plaintiff did not impute the share received by donation from his father is certainly not an indication of inadmissibility...' (page 5 of the brief pursuant to Article 183, paragraph 6, no. 1) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure).

Therefore, the action for reduction must be declared inadmissible and, consequently, any claim relating to the return of the assets must be rejected.

On the claim of simulation relating to the sale of 5 January 2001.

The claim of simulation relating to the sale of 5 January 2001, entered into between **HEIR 4** and his son **HEIR 2**, is instrumental to the action for reduction.

The legitimate heir, who asserts in court his personal right to the intangibility of the legitimate portion and who requests the reinstatement of the reserved portion, is considered a third party with respect to the simulated agreement, since, in this case, he is acting to protect his own right (the right to the intangibility of the reserved portion).

Consequently, "The legitimate heir who requests a declaration of simulation of a sale made by the deceased, aimed at concealing, in reality, a donation, acts to

Page18 of 30

protection of his own right and is a third party with respect to the contracting parties, so that testimonial and presumptive evidence is admissible without limitation when, on the premise that the simulated act involves a reduction in his reserved share, he proposes, at the same time as the action for simulation, a request for reduction of the concealed donation, aimed at having the asset declared part of the estate and his share calculated taking into account the asset itself" (Court of Cassation, Section 2, Judgment No. 19912 of 22/09/2014).

Case law is absolutely consistent and coherent in allowing the (legitimate) heir, in his capacity as a legitimate heir, to act simultaneously in simulation and reduction for the protection of the right to the intangibility of the legitimate portion, to have access to testimonial and presumptive evidence of the simulation agreement in the same way as a third party with respect to the parties who have initiated the simulation proceedings.

That said, it is clear that the close interconnection between the action for reduction and the claim of simulation of a solemn act, such as to allow the person acting in reduction to be admitted to witness evidence, means that the procedural outcome of the latter depends on whether or not the former is upheld.

Therefore, if the action for reduction is not upheld, the legitimate heir cannot be considered a third party and therefore cannot be admitted to testimonial and presumptive evidence.

The simulation will in fact (in the absence of confession and oath) be subject only to documentary evidence by attaching the written text of the simulation agreement (so-called counter-declaration).

In this case, such evidence may be provided by means of texts only in the event of the innocent loss of the document.

It follows that in the case in question, the claim of relative simulation must be rejected because no proof of the actual simulation agreement has been found, whereby the parties would have actually intended to conceal a donation.

On the obligation of collation.

The plaintiffs requested that the court ascertain the existence of the defendant's obligation to collate all the immovable and movable property received by him as a donation and, consequently, order him to transfer it to the estate.

The defendant objected to the admissibility of the request for collation, as it was subject to the acceptance of the request for verification of simulation and verification of the infringement of the legitimate share reserved for **HEIR 3**. Furthermore, in order for

Page19 of 30

collation can proceed, there must be a relictum in addition to the donatum. The former, in light of the plaintiffs' allegations, is absent, because **HEIR 4** died without leaving any assets.

Collation is the act by which the descendants and spouse who accept the inheritance contribute to the estate what they have received from the deceased as a gift.

Collation is based on the assessment that what the deceased has donated to the necessary heirs must be considered an advance on the inheritance and, therefore, this institution aims to remove the disparities in treatment that donations would create between co-heirs.

Collation should not be understood as a tool for reinstating the legitimate portion, even if it may in fact achieve the result of eliminating any damage to the reserved portions caused by acts of generosity carried out by the deceased.

The persons required to make collation are the spouse and descendants who are co-heirs, i.e. who have accepted the inheritance; legitimate heirs who are not co-heirs are not required to make collation until they have successfully brought an action for reduction and obtained the status of heir. Only an action for reduction may be brought against them, if the conditions are met.

That said, in the present case, two successions are relevant, which, for the purposes of the claims for collation, must be analysed separately: on the one hand, the succession of **HEIR 4**, which opened on 27 October 2003 upon his death; on the other hand, the succession of **THE DECEASED**, which opened on 1 February 2000.

The above can be inferred from the following elements:

- the plaintiffs have requested recognition of the defendant's obligation to collate all donations received by him, including those made by his mother;

- they requested that the estate be divided as determined at the time of the opening of the succession;

- in this regard, the writ of summons states 'at the time of the opening of the succession', but the plaintiffs in brief no. 1) pursuant to Article 183 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure specified 'to determine, at the time of the opening of the succession, the estate';

- the reference to both successions can be inferred, in any case, from a systematic reading of the writ of summons, which requests the dissolution of the joint ownership

still existing between the siblings (5/6 for brother **HEIR 2** and 1/6 for the heirs of **HEIR 3**) of the property located in M. inherited following the death of their mother **THE DECEASED**;

- The defendant assumed that both successions were the subject of the proceedings. In fact, in its conclusions in the statement of defence and reply, it requested: 'to proceed with the collation of the donation made in favour of Mr **HEIR 3** and, consequently, with the division of the determined joint inheritance, devolving, with regard to the succession of **THE DECEASED** (50%), 1/3 to Mr **HEIR 3** and 1/3 to Mr **HEIR 2** as legitimate heirs and, with regard to the succession of **HEIR 4** (4/6), the 1/3 share to the heirs of **HEIR 3**..." (page 15 of the statement of defence and reply);

- therefore, all parties requested the collation and division of the joint inheritance in relation to both inheritances;

- consequently, the Court, based on the principle of correspondence between what is requested and what is pronounced, will have to examine and rule on both successions.

With regard to the succession of **HEIR 4**, it appears that:

- This is a testamentary succession by virtue of the holographic will signed by the deceased on 6 July 2000, published by the notary on 8 January 2009, recognised as authentic and valid (see grounds in paragraph 'On the falsity of the holographic will of **HEIR 4** dated 6 July 2000' of this judgment);

- in the aforementioned will, the deceased disposed of all his movable and immovable property, assigning it to his son **HEIR 2**;

- this is a disposition attributing the entirety of the estate, therefore universally representing the appointment of **HEIR 2** as heir;

- the son **HEIR 3**, consequently, can be considered a legitimate heir totally pretermitted by the universal disposition, regardless of the donation received during his parents' lifetime;

- indeed, by virtue of that donation, he was exclusively a donee, while the status of heir is acquired with the call to inheritance at the time of the opening of the succession;

- with the sale on 5 January 2001, he transferred the bare ownership, reserving the usufruct, to his son **HEIR 2** of 4/6 of the property located in M., via (omissis...), thus disposing of all his real estate assets;

- the deceased was the holder of current account no. (omissis...) at the CRC, Montignoso Branch, on which the defendant had power of attorney with separate signature to carry out banking transactions;

- this circumstance was not disputed by the defendant, but was admitted on page 16 of the closing statement ('These amounts were paid in full into deposit book no. 0 (omissis...), held by the second (**HEIR 4**, editor's note) and with separate signing authority granted to the former, as shown in the deposit slips presented by Cassa di Risparmio di Carrara on 23 October 2000 and 8 January 2000', page 16 of the closing statement);

- Finally, **HEIR 4** had inherited from his wife, **THE DECEASED**, 1/3 of the sum contained in passbook no. 421844 at the CRC, Montignoso Agency, which on 7 March 2000 amounted to 13,969 lire (doc. 5, plaintiff's file).

- the withdrawals of money from the savings accounts were admitted by the defendant, who justified them on the grounds of the need to meet the needs and maintenance of his parents, as well as for the improvement and maintenance of the properties available to them;

- the records show several withdrawals from the account (omissis...): on 27 November 2000, a withdrawal of 5,000,000 lire; on 28 May 2001, a withdrawal of 5,000,000 lire; on 30 April 2001 a withdrawal of 6,000,000 lire, but there is also a deposit of 40,000,000 lire by **HEIR 2**, by means of cheques from Monte dei Paschi di Siena;

That said, the Supreme Court of Cassation has consistently held that a pretermitted heir cannot bring an action for collation:

"In matters of inheritance, a pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only after successfully exercising the right of reduction; it follows that, prior to this moment, he or she cannot request the division of the estate or the collation of assets, since both of these rights presuppose the assumption of the status of heir and the joint attribution of an inheritance." (Civil Cassation, Section II, 13/01/2010, no. 368);

"The pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only from the moment of the judgment granting his or her claim for reduction, removing the preclusive effect of the testamentary provisions prejudicial to the legitimate portion, which are not in themselves null and void or voidable;

Page22 of 30

it follows that, prior to the acceptance of the request for reduction, the pretermitted heir is not entitled to succeed the deceased in the legal proceedings initiated by the latter, as he or she cannot be qualified as a universal successor within the meaning of Article 110 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure." (Civil Cassation, Section I, 20/11/2008, no. 27556);

"The pretermitted heir acquires the status of heir only from the moment of the judgment granting his or her request for reduction, removing the preclusive effect of the testamentary dispositions. It follows that, prior to the acceptance of the request for reduction, the pretermitted heir is not entitled to succeed the deceased in the legal proceedings initiated by the latter, since the only person entitled to continue the proceedings, pursuant to Article 110 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, is the universal successor." (Civil Cassation, Section III, 12/01/1999, no. 251).

Therefore, applying the principle established by case law, it follows that:

- the heirs of **HEIR 3** are not entitled to request collation, as their ascendant was a pretermitted heir and the action for reduction brought by them (in their capacity as sole heirs of the same) was unsuccessful, meaning that they did not acquire the status of co-heirs;

- therefore, the claim for collation brought by the plaintiffs must be rejected.

The counterclaim brought by the defendant **HEIR 2** concerning the collation of the donation made by the parents in 1986 in favour of his brother **HEIR 3** must be rejected, again with reference to the paternal succession, as it is subject to the acceptance of the plaintiffs' claim for collation.

Therefore, this claim is absorbed by the rejection of the claims brought by the plaintiffs.

Furthermore, it should be noted that the pretermitted heir is not subject to the obligation of collation, as he is not a co-heir (Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code).

With regard to the sums of money withdrawn by **HEIR 2**, it should be noted that the will attributed to him all immovable and movable property, including, therefore, the sums of money held by the deceased.

Therefore, if the plaintiffs considered themselves to have been harmed in their legitimate share by their father's testamentary dispositions, in order to recover the sums of money contained in the current accounts for the estate, they should have requested, in a counterclaim and, alternatively, the reduction of the testamentary disposition considered harmful (a request that they did not make, on which it is not possible to decide, in accordance with the principle of party disposition and the party's initiative that governs civil proceedings).

Consequently, **HEIR 2** is required to contribute this property, received as a gift, to the estate. Furthermore, since this property has not been sold or mortgaged, as in the present case, the contributor has the choice between contribution in kind (consisting of the

returning the right to the estate) or contribution by imputation (consisting of paying the value of the property).

In this regard, the objections raised by the defendant must be rejected.

In particular, the objection that 'the will must be understood as exempting the latter (**HEIR 2**, editor's note) from the collation of gifts received' is unfounded.

The heir is required to collate the donations, unless he has been exempted by the deceased whose estate is in question. The exemption is an accessory transaction to the donation (contemporary or subsequent), which must take the same form; or it may be contained in a will.

First of all, this concerns the succession of **THE DECEASED**, so the dispensation had to come from the deceased and a dispensation issued by another person cannot be considered valid.

In any case, the will does not contain any express exemption from the obligation of collation and, even if the exemption may also be tacit, it must be able to be inferred unequivocally. For example, the testator should have expressed the obligation solely to his son **HEIR 2**, as can be inferred from the following maxim in terms: 'In the field of negotiation, in order to have a tacit manifestation of the will of a party, 'facta concludentia' are required, i.e. unambiguous and unequivocal, incompatible with a will contrary to that which is argued from it. Such incompatibility does not have to be logical and absolute, as may be given by the principle of contradiction, it being sufficient that it be practical and relative, as results from the predominant concept in practical business life. (In application of the principle referred to in the maxim, the Supreme Court upheld the decision of the trial judge who affirmed the tacit exemption from the obligation of collation of a property by an heir on the grounds that in the same will, this obligation of collation was expressly imposed on another co-heir)" (Civil Cassation, Section II, 08/11/1983, no. 6591).

In light of this jurisprudential principle, elements external to the will reveal an intention that is far from consistent with the decision to exempt the son **HEIR 2** from including the donation received in 1986 in the estate.

Indeed, the fact that two donations were made on that occasion (one to their son **HEIR 3** and one to their son **HEIR 2**) indicates that the deceased did not wish to assign the donated property to **HEIR 2** as an additional benefit on top of his share of the legitimate inheritance.

Finally, the heirs of **HEIR 3** are also required to include in the estate the donation received from their deceased in 1986 concerning 'the entire first floor of the building in

(doc. 3 plaintiff's file).

In fact, the heirs of **HEIR 3**, as legitimate co-heirs together with his brother **HEIR 2** in the maternal succession, are obliged to make a collation (Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code).

On the action for rendering of accounts brought by the plaintiffs.

In the conclusions of the writ of summons, the plaintiffs requested 'the determination, at the time of the opening of the succession, of the estate to be divided, including the accounting of the assets enjoyed by the defendant' (page 8 of the writ of summons).

In particular, they requested an account of the attic of the property in Via (omissis...), which was the subject of the 1986 donation and which, in theory, is a genuine attic floor, which the defendant allegedly enjoyed by renting it to third parties (page 4 of the writ of summons).

With regard to the property sold by **HEIR 4** to his son **HEIR 2**, there is no obligation to provide an account, since, having rejected the claim of simulation, this act must be considered a sale and, therefore, ownership has been transferred and the owner can freely enjoy the property (which is therefore not part of the estate to be divided: the account is in fact instrumental to the division of the estate).

That said, in general terms with regard to the request for an account, the following should be noted:

- first of all, the accounting can only be decided by judgment when the court has already (in the case of an undisputed obligation to account) ordered the obligated party (or parties) to file the statement of account (and the supporting documentation for the assets and liabilities) at least five days before the hearing set for the discussion of the account, at that hearing the party requesting the statement of account has declared that it does not accept it, fulfilling the obligation to indicate the specific items contested and the specific reasons for the contestation, and, at the end of the discussion, the parties have not reached any agreement;

- in the present proceedings, the court has not yet had the opportunity to order any of the parties concerned to file the statement of account and related documentation, so that the proceedings referred to in Article 263 et seq. of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure have not yet commenced;

Page27 of 30

- in accordance with the same Article 723 of the Italian Civil Code, invoked: "After the sale, if it has taken place, of movable or immovable property, the accounts that the co-owners must render shall be settled";

- the same provision, therefore, postpones the rendering of accounts until the conclusion of the sale transactions (where ordered: i.e., in the case of indivisibility in kind of the property and in any case at the request of a party);

- this postponement of the incidental accounting procedure until the conclusion of the sale transactions in the main proceedings for division is shared by specialist doctrine on the subject of divisions;

- consequently, it is necessary to appoint a court-appointed expert to not only estimate the market value of the properties comprising the estate but also to assess whether or not they are divisible in kind and, if so, to draw up a plan for division in kind:

- in the event of indivisibility, in kind, of the estate, the court shall order, solely and exclusively at the request of a party, a judicial sale (which shall follow the new rules that recently came into force in August 2015) and shall appoint a professional to carry out the sale and to take custody of the properties subject to the sale;

- upon completion of the sale, the reconstruction of the estate to be divided shall be completed by means of an incidental accounting procedure, which may result in a negative, positive or zero balance;

- in the event of a specific dispute over the accounting and a persistent lack of agreement even after the hearing to discuss it, the accounting procedure (if any) that has been repeatedly disputed must be settled by means of a judgment;

- the outcome will be the distribution of any remaining assets among the parties involved.

For the reasons set out above, the following ruling does not contain any specific provision relating to the aforementioned request for an account, which is to be understood as included in the provision in which the Court issues, by separate order, separate measures for the investigation of the case.

That said, with regard to the request for division of the inherited assets made by the plaintiff and also requested by the defendants, it will nevertheless be essential to refer the case back to the preliminary investigation stage for the appointment of a new court-appointed expert in order to form the estate, subject to collation by the parties of the two donations made by the deceased on 7 July 1986, relating to the succession of **THE DECEASED**. Consequently, a division plan must be drawn up, on which the parties must agree in accordance with Articles 788 or 789 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure
